symbols.name: first data bank
symbols.meaning: One of the two data banks, with entries X_a.
symbols.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

symbols.name: second data bank
symbols.meaning: The other data bank, with entries Y_a.
symbols.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

symbols.name: bank index
symbols.meaning: A triple of three-element subsets of [h] indexing the entries of the banks.
symbols.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

symbols.name: ground-set size
symbols.meaning: The size of the ground set [h] whose three-element subsets index the banks.
symbols.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and write $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$.

symbols.name: triple set
symbols.meaning: The set of three-element subsets of [h].
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

symbols.name: number of triples
symbols.meaning: The number of three-element subsets of [h].
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

symbols.name: bank size
symbols.meaning: The number of values in each data bank.
symbols.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

symbols.name: label-space dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the label space used on later pages.
symbols.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

symbols.name: invocation count
symbols.meaning: The number of invocations over all three stages.
symbols.quote: A stage covers all $v^2$ choices of the other two coordinates, each with its own invocation and scratch wires, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations.

symbols.name: bit neighbour count
symbols.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the bit construction.
symbols.quote: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction

symbols.name: complex neighbour count
symbols.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
symbols.quote: It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction (intersection zero plus two)

symbols.name: bit central wires
symbols.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the bit network.
symbols.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

symbols.name: complex central wires
symbols.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the complex network.
symbols.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

symbols.name: bit wire count
symbols.meaning: The total number of wires in the bit network.
symbols.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires

symbols.name: complex wire count
symbols.meaning: The total number of wires in the complex network.
symbols.quote: The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires

derivations.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and write $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$. Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.
Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.
A stage covers all $v^2$ choices of the other two coordinates, each with its own invocation and scratch wires, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations.
In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$ and $S,S'$ are neighbours when $|S\cap S'|=1$.

In the complex construction the network keeps its scalars in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, the values of [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md), and the neighbours of a triple are the distinct triples with even intersection (zero or two).

The net change of $y$ is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, free of $\sigma,\gamma$; by the coefficients above it is $y\gets y+x$. So for arbitrary initial scratch values, one forward invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value unchanged

Run forward $X\to Y$ at stage 1, inverse $Y\to X$ at stage 2 and forward $X\to Y$ at stage 3. At every $a$,
$$(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+x)\mapsto(-y,y+x)\mapsto(-y,x),$$
that is $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$
A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction
It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction (intersection zero plus two)
There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.
The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires
The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires
